next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: California Secretary of State — General Election, November 3, 2026

glance_notes.source_name: California Secretary of State — Ways to Vote
glance_notes.text: Vote-by-Mail Ballots: Every active registered California voter will be mailed a vote-by-mail ballot for the November 3, 2026 General Election.

glance_notes.source_name: California Secretary of State — Same Day Voter Registration
glance_notes.text: Same Day Voter Registration: Eligible Californians who miss the regular registration deadline can use Same Day Voter Registration, called Conditional Voter Registration in state law, during the final 14 days before an election through Election Day.

glance_notes.source_name: California Secretary of State — Election Dates and Resources
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The regular voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 19, 2026. Eligible voters who miss that deadline can use Same Day Voter Registration.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible California residents can register to vote online through the California Secretary of State or complete a paper Voter Registration Card. To register, you must be a United States citizen and California resident, be at least 18 years old on Election Day, not currently be serving a state or federal prison term for a felony conviction, and not currently have been found mentally incompetent to vote by a court. The registration application asks for a California driver license or state identification number, or the last four digits of your Social Security number if you do not have a California ID. If you have none of these numbers, you can still register and election officials will assign an identifier.
register.source_name: California Secretary of State — California Online Voter Registration
register.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: California Secretary of State Voter Registration — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration) — supports eligibility requirements and registration identification procedures. Registration identification requirements are distinct from identification requirements when casting a ballot.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use California's My Voter Status tool to check your voter registration. The tool allows voters to verify their registration information and voting status. You can also contact your county elections office if you have questions about your registration.
check_registration.source_name: California Secretary of State — My Voter Status
check_registration.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: California Secretary of State Elections — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections) — directs voters to My Voter Status to determine whether they are currently registered. Secretary of State FAQ also confirms voters may check registration through My Voter Status or their county elections official.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: The regular voter registration deadline in California is 15 days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, online registration must be completed or a mailed registration must be postmarked by October 19, 2026. If you miss that deadline, eligible voters can use Same Day Voter Registration, legally known as Conditional Voter Registration, during the final 14 days before the election through Election Day at qualifying locations.
deadlines.source_name: California Secretary of State — Election Dates and Resources
deadlines.internal_note: Primary source expressly lists October 19, 2026 as the online/postmark registration deadline for the November 3 General Election and notes conditional registration after the 15-day deadline. Additional verification source: California Secretary of State Same Day Voter Registration — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration/same-day-reg](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration/same-day-reg) — establishes availability to eligible citizens within 14 days of an election.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use the California Secretary of State's official polling-place lookup to find your voting location. Polling locations are established by county elections officials. The Secretary of State's lookup can also direct voters to ballot information and election-official contact information. Early voting, vote-center, Same Day Voter Registration, and ballot drop-off locations can be found through the state's early-voting locator or your county elections office.
polling_place.source_name: California Secretary of State — Find Your Polling Place
polling_place.internal_note: The official lookup directly supports polling-place searches and directs voters to CAEarlyVoting for early voting, Same Day Voter Registration, and drop-off locations.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: California voters can vote in person on Election Day. Polling locations are established by county elections officials. If you received a vote-by-mail ballot but decide to vote in person instead, you may still vote at a polling location. If necessary, election officials can use provisional voting procedures to ensure an eligible voter has an opportunity to cast a ballot while eligibility or prior voting is verified. Eligible voters who missed the regular registration deadline can also use Same Day Voter Registration at qualifying Election Day locations.
election_day.source_name: California Secretary of State — Ways to Vote
election_day.internal_note: Supplemental verification source for voting after receiving a mail ballot and provisional voting: California Secretary of State — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/voting-california/if-you-applied](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/voting-california/if-you-applied). Supplemental source for Same Day Voter Registration: [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration/same-day-reg](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration/same-day-reg).

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: California polling locations are open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the statewide polling hours are 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
polling_hours.source_name: California Secretary of State — 2026 General Election Key Dates and Deadlines
polling_hours.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current 2026 General Election page expressly states that polls shall be open throughout California from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on November 3, 2026.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: California offers in-person voting before Election Day. County elections officials offer early voting at their offices, and many counties provide additional early-voting locations. Locations and schedules vary by county. In counties operating under the Voter's Choice Act, vote centers begin opening for the November 3, 2026 General Election on October 24. Statewide early-voting locations will also be available on Saturday, October 31. Use the state's early-voting locator or contact your county elections office for current locations and hours.
early_voting.source_name: California Secretary of State — Early Voting and Vote-by-Mail Drop-Off Locations
early_voting.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: California Secretary of State Ways to Vote — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-info/ways-vote](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-info/ways-vote) — states county elections officials offer early voting at their offices and many counties offer additional locations. California Secretary of State Make a Plan to Vote — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/make-plan-vote](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/make-plan-vote) — establishes October 24 as the first day vote centers open in Voter's Choice Act counties for the 2026 General Election and October 31 for statewide Saturday early-voting availability. Hours and locations are locally administered and should not be generalized statewide.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: California mails a vote-by-mail ballot to every active registered voter; no excuse is required. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, you can return your completed ballot by mail, at an official drop box, at a voting location, or to a county elections office. Personally delivered ballots must be returned by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. A mailed ballot must be postmarked on or before November 3 and received by the county elections office no later than November 10. California also allows another person to return your ballot as permitted by state law. Voters can track their mailed ballot using the statewide Where's My Ballot service.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Ballot mailed to every active registered voter
absentee_mail.source_name: California Secretary of State — Ways to Vote
absentee_mail.internal_note: Additional verification source for November 3/November 10 return deadlines: California Secretary of State Election Dates and Resources — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/voting-california/election-dates-and-resources](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/voting-california/election-dates-and-resources). Additional verification source for ballot tracking: California Secretary of State Where's My Ballot — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/ballot-status/wheres-my-ballot](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/ballot-status/wheres-my-ballot). Secretary of State Where and How to Vote — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/where-and-how](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/where-and-how) — supports authorized third-party return and explains signature verification.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: California generally does not require voters to show identification at the polls. An identification requirement can apply when you are voting for the first time in a federal election, registered by mail or online, and did not provide a California driver license or state identification number or the required Social Security number information when registering. If identification is required, California accepts qualifying photo and non-photo documents, including a driver's license or state ID, U.S. passport, student or military ID, utility bill, bank statement, paycheck, government check, or qualifying official government mail. Poll workers may request identification only when the voter record indicates that it is required.
voter_id.glance_value: No ID at polls in most cases
voter_id.source_name: California Secretary of State — Where and How to Vote
voter_id.internal_note: The current Secretary of State page directly establishes California's general no-ID-at-polls rule, the limited first-time federal voter exception, and examples of acceptable photo and non-photo identification. California Secretary of State Voter Registration — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration) — independently states the same distinction. Registration identification requirements are intentionally kept separate from voting identification requirements.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: California polling places and vote centers are required to be accessible to voters with disabilities and provide accessible voting machines. A voter who needs help marking a ballot may choose up to two people to assist, except the voter's employer, someone working for the employer, the voter's labor union leader, or someone working for that union. California also offers Remote Accessible Vote-by-Mail, which allows voters to access and mark a ballot using compatible technology at home, then print and return the ballot by mail or in person. A Remote Accessible Vote-by-Mail ballot cannot be returned electronically.
accessible_voting.source_name: California Secretary of State — Voters with Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: Primary source establishes polling-place/vote-center accessibility, accessible machines, and voter-assistance rules. Additional verification source: California Secretary of State Remote Accessible Vote-by-Mail — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/remote-accessible-vote-mail](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/remote-accessible-vote-mail) — explains RAVBM operation and confirms marked selections must be printed and returned physically rather than electronically.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Eligible California military and overseas voters can register using California's online voter registration system or the Federal Post Card Application and receive voting materials while away from their county or living overseas. Military and overseas voters are automatically sent vote-by-mail ballots after registering in this status. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, ballots for military and overseas voters who requested them by the applicable deadline must be transmitted no later than September 19. A ballot returned by mail must be postmarked on or before Election Day and received by the county elections office no later than seven days after Election Day. California also permits eligible military and overseas voters to return a ballot by fax under specified circumstances directly to their county elections official.
military_overseas.source_name: California Secretary of State — Military & Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Primary source directly supports registration, mailed ballot return deadlines, and military/overseas procedures. Additional verification source: 2026 General Election Key Dates and Deadlines — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/upcoming-elections/general-election-november-3-2026/key-dates-deadlines](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/upcoming-elections/general-election-november-3-2026/key-dates-deadlines) — establishes September 19, 2026 as the federal 45-day ballot-transmission deadline. Additional official source for county-specific fax return information: [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration/military-overseas-voters/mailing-military-or-overseas-voters](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voter-registration/military-overseas-voters/mailing-military-or-overseas-voters). Fax return is subject to special requirements and should not be presented as equivalent to ordinary vote-by-mail return.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A California resident living away from home while attending college, trade school, or technical school may choose to register using the address where they live while attending school or their traditional home address. The choice is the student's, but a voter may not register to vote in two places during the same election cycle. Students otherwise follow California's normal eligibility and registration rules. Students temporarily living outside the United States can use the military and overseas voter procedures when eligible.
student_voting.glance_value: Register at school or traditional home
student_voting.source_name: California Secretary of State — College Students and Voters Living Abroad
student_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State page directly establishes the choice between a school-area residence and traditional home address and states that a student may not register in two places during the same election cycle. California Students Vote Project — [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/castudentsvote](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/castudentsvote) — independently confirms standard registration eligibility for college students.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: California voters receive a County Voter Information Guide that contains a sample of their ballot and information about local candidates and ballot measures. For statewide elections, the Secretary of State also publishes an Official State Voter Information Guide covering statewide candidates and statewide ballot measures. The state's polling-place lookup can also show what is on the ballot based on a voter's address when election information is available.
sample_ballot.glance_value: County guide contains your sample ballot
sample_ballot.source_name: California Secretary of State — State Voter Information Guide vs. County Voter Information Guide
sample_ballot.internal_note: Primary source expressly states that the County Voter Information Guide, formerly called the sample ballot, contains a sample of the voter's ballot plus local candidate and measure information. Statewide guide source: [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/voter-information-guides](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/voter-information-guides) — includes the November 3, 2026 General Election. Polling-place lookup source: [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/polling-place](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/polling-place).

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: California Secretary of State, Elections Division, 1500 11th Street, 5th Floor, Sacramento, CA 95814. The Elections Division phone number is 916-657-2166. The statewide English Voter Hotline is 800-345-VOTE (8683), and the Secretary of State provides additional voter hotlines in multiple languages as well as 711 TTY/TDD service. Office hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding state holidays.
contact.source_name: California Secretary of State — Elections Contact Information
contact.internal_note: The official Elections Division contact page directly verifies the address, office hours, Elections Division telephone number, English voter hotline, multilingual voter hotlines, and 711 TTY/TDD service. The Secretary of State uses an official web contact form for Elections Division email inquiries rather than publishing a general Elections Division email address on this page.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the California Secretary of State Elections website for statewide voting information, RegisterToVote.ca.gov to register online, My Voter Status to check your registration, and the Secretary of State's polling-place and early-voting tools to locate voting services. California elections are administered locally by county elections officials, and the Secretary of State maintains an official directory with contact information and links for every county elections office.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State & county elections offices
official_resources.source_name: California Secretary of State — Elections and Voter Information
official_resources.internal_note: Official online registration: [https://registertovote.ca.gov/](https://registertovote.ca.gov/). Official registration-status tool: [https://voterstatus.sos.ca.gov/](https://voterstatus.sos.ca.gov/). Official polling-place lookup: [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/polling-place](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/polling-place). Official early-voting locator: [https://caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov/](https://caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov/). Official county elections office directory: [https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/county-elections-offices](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/voting-resources/county-elections-offices). These are all California government election resources.
